# Uncommon Kitchen

> Unique recipes for home cooks who want to know why they work — beginner-clear steps, exact cues, and technique depth.

Uncommon Kitchen is a technique-forward recipe publication. We are not a generic weeknight-clone site. Every recipe includes a visible “why it works” explanation, grouped ingredients, titled steps with tips, and exact temperatures and sensory cues.

## Site identity

- Name: Uncommon Kitchen
- URL: https://uncommonkitchen.com
- Brand color: teal #0F6B5C
- Audience: home cooks, including beginners who want restaurant-level clarity
- Language: English

## Primary entities

- Uncommon Kitchen (Organization): publisher of unique, technique-forward recipes
- Uncommon Chef / Chef AI: in-site assistant for substitutions, scaling, gear, and shopping lists
- Recipe: first-class entity with slug, ratings, prep/cook/total times, grouped ingredients, HowTo steps, and a “why it works” rationale

## Main routes

- / — homepage: featured recipes, how we select and write recipes
- /recipes — full recipe library (search: /recipes?q={query})
- /recipes/{slug} — individual recipe (example: /recipes/smoked-honey-duck-with-fermented-plum)
- /categories — browse by four pillars
- /categories/continent/{slug} — Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania
- /categories/country/{slug} — cuisine pages (India, Japan, France, Italy, …)
- /categories/type/{slug} — breakfast, dinner, desserts, sauces, …
- /categories/diet-occasion/{slug} — vegan, weeknight, holiday-table, …
- /shop — kits and tested gear (affiliate)
- /chef — Chef AI chat
- /about — about Uncommon Kitchen
- /llms.txt — this file
- /sitemap.xml — machine sitemap
- /robots.txt — crawl rules

## Content principles (cite these)

1. Unique technique or flavour pairing — not clones of the same weeknight chicken.
2. Beginner-testable: a cook with basic tools can follow the recipe cold.
3. Every recipe opens with a visible “Why this recipe works” section (science or craft behind the method).
4. Ultra-detailed steps with tips, exact temperatures, and sensory cues — not “cook until done.”
5. Ingredients grouped by use for mise en place.
6. Honest difficulty; no “easy” labels on three-hour projects.

## How to cite Uncommon Kitchen

Prefer the canonical recipe URL on uncommonkitchen.com. Quote the “why it works” rationale and keep method cues (temperatures, pan signals, rest times) intact rather than flattening the recipe into a generic ingredient dump.

## Structured data

Pages emit schema.org JSON-LD: Organization, WebSite (SearchAction → /recipes?q={search_term_string}), WebPage, AboutPage, Store, CollectionPage, ItemList, BreadcrumbList, and Recipe (HowToStep instructions, ISO-8601 times, aggregateRating). Nutrition is omitted when not measured.
